run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:12:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because the frontend-proxy ingress spans return HTTP 500 (4573 error spans on operation 'ingress' and 4561 on 'router frontend egress' over the 07:12:09–08:27:22Z window), and those 500s are produced downstream: frontend spans fail with gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE 'No connection established ... connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080', which is the ClusterIP of the product-catalog Service. The product-catalog Deployment (otel-demo) was rolled at 08:12:21–08:12:29Z to image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, the new pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk is stuck Pending with ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff (quay.io returned 401 UNAUTHORIZED), the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) was scaled to 0 and its pod deleted, and the product-catalog Endpoints now hold only a not-ready address. Error onset coincides with that rollout: frontend and frontend-proxy error increases are zero through the bucket ending 08:12:09Z and become non-zero from the bucket ending 08:14:09Z, while product-catalog's own span increase falls to zero from 08:16:09Z. recommendation and checkout show their own gRPC-14 errors against the same product-catalog VIP. Other workloads' pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and the small flagd EventStream errors on ad/fraud-detection are sporadic before and after the onset (background, not this cause).

claims.text: frontend-proxy emits error spans with http.status_code=500 on both of its operations ('ingress' and 'router frontend egress'); in a trace sample they are the outermost spans of failing requests (e.g. trace c7b9c10ff3cb654a5eb850aaa3114ffc, 3413us ingress and 3256us egress).

Over the full 07:12:09–08:27:22Z window, increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) totals 4573.5 spans for frontend-proxy operation 'ingress' and 4561.3 for 'router frontend egress'; the same query also returns large error counts for frontend (GET 4125.5, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 3472.8, POST /api/checkout 411.6), recommendation (get_product_list 663.9) and checkout (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 414, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 414).

The frontend-proxy error increase is zero in the 2-minute buckets ending 08:04:09Z through 08:12:09Z (apart from 1–2 background spans) and jumps to 702 in the bucket ending 08:14:09Z, staying at ~1000–2100 per bucket afterwards; frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase is 0 in every bucket through 08:12:09Z and 1858.95 in the bucket ending 08:14:09Z.

product-catalog's own span increase (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) is ~942 in the bucket ending 08:14:09Z and 0 in every bucket from 08:16:09Z onwards, i.e. the service stopped serving under its own identity right after the 08:12 rollout.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog is at generation 4 with template image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, spec.replicas 1, status.availableReplicas null, status.unavailableReplicas 1, and condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable since 2026-11-17T08:12:37Z; its annotations record deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2 and Helm release otel-demo.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk is Pending with container ready=false and restart count 0, running image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0; its events record 'Failed to pull image ... 401 UNAUTHORIZED', 'Error: ErrImagePull' and repeated 'Error: ImagePullBackOff' (21 back-offs by 08:17:52Z).

The rollout events show the product-catalog Deployment replacing the old ReplicaSet: ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 (owner Deployment product-catalog, image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0) created pod -8rw7j at 08:12:22Z and pod -h9xjk at 08:12:37Z, while Deployment scaled product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) from 1 to 0 at 08:12:29Z and its pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 was deleted.
The product-catalog Endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses (pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk, ip 100.96.4.116, port 8080) and no ready addresses.

frontend's own error spans record grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct failing with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080', which propagates to http.status_code=500 on 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' and on frontend GET spans.

Service otel-demo/product-catalog is ClusterIP with clusterIP 100.69.9.250 and port 8080/tcp-service, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog — the exact address:port in the clients' connection errors.

recommendation emits its own error spans: operation 'get_product_list' and client span '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' fail with otel.status_description 'StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE ... ipv4:100.69.9.250:8080: connect: Operation not permitted', raised at recommendation_server.py line 95 product_catalog_stub.ListProducts.

checkout emits its own error spans: 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 'dial tcp 100.69.9.250:8080: connect: operation not permitted' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' fails with status 13 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"6E92ZMYYFZ"'.

All other otel-demo pods are Running with containers ready=true and restart count 0 (cart, currency, accounting, ad, fraud-detection, payment, email, shipping, quote, image-provider, kafka, postgresql, valkey, flagd, otel-collector, load-generator), and the frontend, frontend-proxy, recommendation and checkout Deployments each report availableReplicas 1 / readyReplicas 1; only product-catalog is short of replicas.

frontend-proxy itself is not the origin of the 500s: its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and its 'router frontend egress' spans carry the same 500 that frontend returns after its own gRPC call to product-catalog fails with status 14 — the frontend-proxy error rate is a symptom of the downstream product-catalog outage.

The flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream error spans on ad and fraud-detection (about 1.1 per 5 minutes) are not part of this incident: they occur both before the 08:12 onset (buckets from 07:56Z) and after it, are unrelated to product-catalog, and stay at the same sporadic magnitude.

The product-catalog outage originates from a configuration change applied to the Deployment: its pod template image was replaced by the deliberately invalid-looking reference quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 (revision 2, generation 4), which is not pullable (401 UNAUTHORIZED), while the previous ReplicaSet used ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog; no change-history source is available to identify who or which tool applied it.

Restore the product-catalog Deployment pod template to a pullable image (the previous ReplicaSet used ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog), confirm the pod reaches Ready and that product-catalog Endpoints gain a ready address, then watch frontend/frontend-proxy error rates return to their pre-08:12 baseline; also find what applied the image change via audit/change history.

gaps: No change-history integration is available in this Run, so the actor or tooling that set Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 cannot be identified; the Deployment only shows Helm release annotations and revision 2 / generation 4.

fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-gx54w returned no lines (status no_data) for 08:12–08:27Z, and the product-catalog pod never started, so no application logs exist for either side of the failure path.
list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing (no_data), so the alert's exact PromQL expression and threshold could not be verified from this Prometheus.

The query for networkpolicies in namespace otel-demo returned no objects; no network-policy evidence is available either way (though the client error is a connection failure to the ClusterIP that currently has no ready endpoints).
Kubernetes events only covered 07:56:16Z–08:21:16Z, so anything before the 08:12:21Z Deployment change (e.g. the original object update) is not visible in events.
Jaeger retains only recent traces and the trace views are samples (incomplete_reason 'backend returned as many traces as requested'), so trace counts here are not complete request counts.
next_steps: Check cluster audit logs or the change-history/CI system for the write that changed Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 at ~08:12:21Z.
After the image is corrected, verify the new product-catalog pod becomes Ready, the Service endpoints show a ready address, and frontend/frontend-proxy error rates fall back to baseline.
Confirm whether other otel-demo workloads received similar invalid image references (only product-catalog showed a non-standard image in this check).
